title: The Nanofabbed Atlas of Fourier Transforms: Interactive Diffraction Education
content: The Fourier transform is ubiquitous, appearing at the heart of electron microscopy, materials science, quantum physics, biology, computer science, and electrical engineering. An accessible intuition for the Fourier transform is invaluable for the development of new theories and the processing of data. However, mastery of diffraction and Fourier transforms requires extensive practice [1-3], and the development of Fourier space expertise can be a significant barrier for new scientists and curious students.
